html:
The first emperor of Nicaea, from 1205 to 1221. He founded the Byzantine state in exile that later won back Constantinople.

He was son in law of Emperor Alexios III Angelos. When the Fourth Crusade took Constantinople in 1204, he crossed into Anatolia and gathered the Greek cities there under his rule, making Nicaea his capital. He was crowned emperor, and the patriarch moved to Nicaea, which gave the new state the claim to be the true empire.

He had enemies on two sides. The Latin Empire in Constantinople beat him in battle in 1211 and took land, but could not destroy him. The same year he defeated the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum at Antioch on the Meander, where the sultan was killed. He died in 1221 and was followed by his son in law John III Vatatzes, who made the Empire of Nicaea the strongest of the Greek successor states.
sum: The first emperor of Nicaea, from 1205 to 1221. He founded the Byzantine state in exile that later won back Constantinople.
